summary: A VS Code extension that keeps cSpell custom words in sync between every project and the global dictionary, in both directions. Words added in one project reach the global list within a second, so opening a new project no longer means red squiggles under your whole technical vocabulary.
highlights: Reads from four sources — project settings, custom dictionaries, language-specific settings and combined.txt drop files — and merges them into the global word list.
Bidirectional: global words can be pushed back into a project, workspace, existing dictionary or a new dictionary file.
A debounced watcher on .vscode/settings.json syncs a newly added word within one second.
Bundles to roughly 30 KB with zero runtime npm dependencies, and activates on onStartupFinished so it never delays editor startup.

sections.heading: Design constraints
items: Activation on onStartupFinished — a spell-checker helper must never be on the startup critical path.
A two-tier settings cache with a 30-second TTL, so unchanged JSON is not reparsed on every keystroke.
Incremental sync that processes only the changed settings file rather than every workspace folder.
